_comment: Sole source for every duration and control-point number the theme-engine emits (D-05). Every consumer resolves a semantic name — never a copied/inlined literal. The 'motion-' prefix on emitted Hyprland curve names is a deliberate collision guard against animations.conf's 12 hand-authored beziers (D-04: additive only, nothing rewired this phase).
_comment_13_07_removal: 13-07 removed D-21's temporary A/B curve-comparison toggle (the top-level object that used to sit here, named 'curve' + '_sets') and D-11's marked non-MD3 'x-' prefixed easing extension (the five character curves this project's default vocabulary never adopted) — no D-22 retune ever adopted any of them, because the soak gate that would have produced a retune verdict was waived by explicit operator decision rather than passed (see 13-MOTION-SOAK-VERDICT.md). The six feel-changing Hyprland slots (windows-in/out/move, fade-in/out, workspaces) that used to read the removed per-slot curve variable now reference the toggle's former MD3-default mapping directly as literals in animations.conf. The shipped easing vocabulary below is pure MD3.
_comment_260821_swp_reversal: quick-260821-swp reinstates, as a genuine user-facing setting, the kind of per-style curve data plan 13-07 removed above as a measuring instrument — this time under a 'styles' table rather than a temporary A/B toggle, and never re-adopting the deleted 'x-' character easings by name. TOKEN-06's 'MD3 is better, spring is too fast' verdict was a tuning-parameter rejection, not a mechanism rejection (a future spring revisit was explicitly left open) — this task does not revisit springs, it revisits SHAPE via bezier-only per-style curves (R-1), so neither prior decision is being overturned, only the axis this repo exposes to the user.
_comment_spatial_easings: spatial-in/spatial-out/spatial-move (R-2) are the ONLY three easing names a style may ever push a control-point Y above 1.0 on — every other name below stays monotonic within [0,1] in every style, forever, so a fade or a colour can never be given overshoot by construction. Seeded here identical to emphasized-decelerate/emphasized-accelerate/standard so this task's Task 1 restructure moves nothing on screen; Task 2 gives each non-md3 style its own points for these three names only.
_comment_semantic_leaf_channels: semantic's last two entries (emphasized-decelerate / emphasized-accelerate) are LEAF-ONLY channels. They exist so a style can give a Hyprland leaf a curve+speed pair the four shared channels (standard/spatial-in/spatial-out/spatial-move) cannot express: animations.lua derives a leaf's speed from its CURVE NAME (register_hypr_leaf: speed_key = curve:gsub('-','_')), so two leaves sharing a curve are forced onto one duration, and these names break that tie without disturbing a shared channel. Inert until a hypr_leaves entry names them - no base leaf does, and Motion.qml walks a FIXED _pairNames list, so they reach neither QML nor any existing style. NOTE: every key inside 'semantic' MUST be a {duration,easing} object, never a comment string - lib/motion.sh renders it with `.semantic | to_entries[] | $D[$v.duration]`, which a string value breaks. Added 2026-08-25 for 'zen'.
_comment_accessibility: The reduced-motion/animations-off axis, orthogonal to style (BRIEF: 'off'/'reduced' do NOT become styles). Same {multiplier, animations_enabled} shape the removed 'scales' table carried, so every reader below the resolution point (Motion.qml's ambientDuration divide-back-out logic, the gate's scaled-speed forgiveness) needs no rewrite. 'lively' (1.25x) has no home here — the multiplier axis is absorbed by per-style durations; a legacy 'lively' value migrates to style md3 + accessibility full (a deliberate, stated loss).
_comment_hypr_leaves: One entry per style-varying Hyprland leaf. Fade/border/borderangle leaves are deliberately absent — they keep their hardcoded wiring in animations.lua (a style changes window/workspace ENTRY SHAPE and curve, never a fade's style string or borderangle's loop mechanism). Seeded here identical to today's animations.lua literals, with the spatial curve names substituted for the emphasized-decelerate/emphasized-accelerate/standard names those leaves used before this task.
_comment_styles: Each style may override a SUBSET of easings/semantic/hypr_leaves keys (schema invariant: override keys must be a subset of the base table's keys — a style changes points behind a name, never adds a name). Overrides are shallow-merged over the base tables at render/gate time — a style-provided key replaces its base entry wholesale, a key the style does not mention keeps the base value. 'style' strings reach Hyprland's own parser directly, so each must match ^[a-z]+( [0-9]{1,3}%)?$.

md3.label: MD3
md3.description: Decelerate, lands exactly, no overshoot — today's shipped behaviour, unchanged.

snappy.label: Snappy
snappy.description: Short, fast rise, a barely-there overshoot.

bouncy.label: Bouncy
bouncy.description: Crests past the target, drops back through it, then settles — the snap-back of a bounce.
bouncy._comment_curve: This dipping curve carries a history worth knowing before retuning it. (1) Hyprland's hl.curve() rejects any control-point Y above 2.00 and then SILENTLY KEEPS the previously registered curve instead of failing the reload — an out-of-range number looks exactly like 'my edit did nothing'. (2) It first shipped as [0.05, 2.0, 0.3, 0.6] and was rejected by the operator on 2026-08-22 as causing motion sickness: it fired its whole +10.8% overshoot in the first 94ms of 450ms — already 111% of the way by a fifth of the duration — then sagged to 8% BELOW the target for the remaining 356ms. (3) A retune to [0.3, 1.45, 0.7, 0.94] at +4% overcorrected and read as a near-twin of smooth. What those verdicts together establish is that neither the crest SIZE nor the 450ms length was the problem — the SNAP was, together with the sag depth and the fact that the reversal landed on a whole-screen vertical slide. [0.4, 1.85, 0.75, 0.74] keeps the crest (+9.7%) but reaches it smoothly at 54% of the duration and dips only 4.2%. (4) It lived under the 'wavy' name until 2026-08-22, when the operator judged the two names backwards — a curve that overshoots and comes BACK DOWN reads as a bounce, not a wave — and the curves were swapped. The motion moved; this history moved with it.
bouncy._comment_leaves: workspaces/special_workspace MUST stay on a monotonic curve while this style owns the dipping spatial-in. They keep their vertical slidevert shape, but on spatial-move rather than spatial-in. This is not stylistic: the operator's motion sickness came from a reversing curve landing on a whole-screen VERTICAL slide, and this style is the one that puts full-screen motion on spatial-in. Vertical motion itself was never the trigger — this style ran a full-screen vertical slidevert with a +8% monotonic overshoot for weeks without complaint — so the shape stays and only the reversal is kept off it. special_workspace needs an explicit override here because the BASE table points it at spatial-in. Note a leaf's DURATION follows its curve name (animations.lua register_hypr_leaf: speed_key = curve name), so this also moves workspace switching onto spatial-move's 200ms.

wavy.label: Wavy
wavy.description: One smooth swell past the target, settling from above — never doubles back.
wavy._comment_curve: Held the dipping wave curve until 2026-08-22, when the operator judged the wavy/bouncy names backwards and the two curves were swapped — a dip-and-return reads as a bounce, a single smooth swell reads as a wave. The full history of the dipping curve now lives under 'bouncy'. [0.1, 0.9, 0.4, 1.254] peaks +8.0% at 66% of the duration and settles from above without ever crossing back below the target.
wavy._comment_leaves: workspaces/special_workspace use spatial-move with a vertical slidefadevert. This style no longer carries a reversing curve (that moved to 'bouncy' in the 2026-08-22 name swap), so the split is now about pacing rather than safety: full-screen motion runs at spatial-move's 250ms while windows and panels swell over 350ms. Keep the shape here distinct from smooth's horizontal slidefade — an earlier pass made these leaves horizontal and the operator reported the style then read as smooth. Note a leaf's DURATION follows its curve name (animations.lua register_hypr_leaf: speed_key = curve name).

zen.label: Zen
zen.description: Caelestia's motion, reproduced exactly — unhurried, gliding, no overshoot anywhere.
zen._comment_provenance: EXACT PORT of caelestia-dots/caelestia hypr/hyprland/animations.lua (read 2026-08-25 via the GitHub contents API). Every one of the eight style-controlled Hyprland leaves below reproduces its Caelestia counterpart's curve AND speed exactly. Caelestia's speeds are deciseconds (confirmed on this host: hyprctl animations reports layersIn 4.50 for a 450ms leaf), so 5 = 500ms. Source values: layersIn 5/emphasizedDecel/slide, layersOut 4/emphasizedAccel/slide, windowsIn 5/emphasizedDecel/no style, windowsOut 3/emphasizedAccel/no style, windowsMove 6/standard/no style, workspaces 5/standard/no style, specialWorkspace 4/specialWorkSwitch/slidefadevert 15%.
zen._comment_curves: This style overrides NO easings, and that is a measured result rather than an omission: all four of Caelestia's curves are already BYTE-IDENTICAL to this repo's base easings. Caelestia 'standard' {0.2,0},{0,1} == our standard == our spatial-move; 'emphasizedDecel' {0.05,0.7},{0.1,1} == our emphasized-decelerate == our spatial-in; 'emphasizedAccel' {0.3,0},{0.8,0.15} == our emphasized-accelerate == our spatial-out; and 'specialWorkSwitch' is a byte-for-byte duplicate of emphasizedDecel. What makes Caelestia feel like Caelestia is duration and leaf shape, not curvature.
zen._comment_channels: WHY THE LEAVES BELOW POINT AT SIX DIFFERENT CURVE NAMES FOR ONLY THREE DISTINCT CURVES: animations.lua derives a leaf's speed from its curve name (register_hypr_leaf: speed_key = curve:gsub('-','_')), so two leaves sharing a curve name are forced onto one duration. Caelestia needs six distinct curve+speed pairs — emphasizedDecel@500, emphasizedAccel@300, emphasizedAccel@400, standard@600, standard@500, emphasizedDecel@400 — and only four shared channels existed, which is why base 'semantic' gained the two leaf-only channels emphasized-decelerate/emphasized-accelerate. Each leaf is routed to a channel whose POINTS already equal the Caelestia curve it must reproduce, so no easing override is needed: windowsIn/layersIn -> emphasized-decelerate@500, windowsOut -> spatial-out@300, layersOut -> emphasized-accelerate@400, windowsMove -> standard@600, workspaces -> spatial-move@500, specialWorkspace -> spatial-in@400.
zen._comment_standard_600: standard=600ms is Caelestia's own value and is deliberately NOT decoupled. On the Hyprland side it is exactly right: it drives windowsMove (Caelestia 6) and fadeDim (Caelestia 6), and fadeSwitch/fadeShadow, which Caelestia leaves at Hyprland defaults, follow the same channel here. THE COST, stated plainly: Motion.standardDuration is this same token, so every QML surface bound to it also runs at 600ms while Zen is active. Decoupling would need a THIRD base easing carrying {0.2,0},{0,1} purely so windowsMove could hold 600 while QML kept a shorter standard — a new name in the base easings table, registered as a live Hyprland curve on every style, to serve one leaf. Judged not worth it; revisit if the shell reads sluggish under Zen.
zen._comment_unspecified: emphasized-in/emphasized-out are deliberately NOT overridden. They drive Hyprland's fadeIn/fadeOut, which Caelestia does not configure at all — inheriting the base values is the faithful reading of 'unspecified', not a gap.
zen._comment_leaves: windows_in/windows_out/windows_move/workspaces carry a curve but NO style key, reproducing Caelestia exactly: its window and workspace leaves pass no style, so Hyprland's own default applies. register_hypr_leaf only sets args.style when entry.style ~= nil, and a style's leaf entry REPLACES the base entry wholesale, so omitting the key here genuinely drops base's 'popin 60%'/'slide' rather than inheriting it. The parent 'layers' leaf has no Caelestia counterpart (its config declares only layersIn/layersOut/fadeLayers); it mirrors layersIn so the inheritance slot stays declared, as the animations.lua comment requires.
